title: Starlink satellites made 207,152 evasive moves without a single human pilot
title_candidates: Starlink satellites made 207,152 evasive moves without a single human pilot
How Starlink's AI decides when to move a satellite out of the way
Every Starlink satellite in orbit is dodging debris on its own, right now
The invisible system stopping Starlink from crashing into itself
SpaceX built a system that runs 1,100 space dodges a day, fully automatic
caption:
SpaceX's Starlink network made 207,152 autonomous collision-avoidance maneuvers in just six months. No human approved a single one.

Each satellite runs its own system that detects a nearby object, calculates how dangerous it is, and fires thrusters to move out of the way, all without waiting for anyone on the ground. That process runs constantly, across hundreds of satellites at once, in a part of space that gets more crowded every year.

Without it, a constellation this big would eventually crash into itself and block everyone below from using that orbit at all.
